security_review.reason: Required from THIS registration's start, not carved as an exception: the second registration's own security_review.reason contained a material measurement error, corrected here. That reason claimed 'the pre-existing message already interpolates the full stringified error... nothing newly reaches a consumer the message did not already carry' -- FALSE. Measured 2026-08-01: String(error) (the OLD, pre-any-of-this-slice's-work path) renders only the top-level `"${name}: ${message}"`. What migrate.ts's CLI now prints via console.error(wrappingError) additionally surfaces the ENTIRE pg DatabaseError shape via Node's default .cause-recursive formatting: severity, code, detail, hint, position, internalPosition, internalQuery, where, schema, table, column, dataType, constraint, file, line, routine. The earlier claim conflated 'the error object's enumerable key set' (correctly measured: no .client, no credentials) with 'what String(error) actually renders' (a much narrower thing, never separately verified until this registration) -- two different measurements collapsed into one. Worse: `detail` specifically is NOT schema/DDL-shaped like the rest of that list -- on a unique-violation Postgres populates it with the OFFENDING ROW'S ACTUAL VALUES, e.g. `Key (email)=(user@example.com) already exists.`. A migration performing a data backfill against tables like persons/accounts/channel_identities would print real PII into deployment logs. That collides directly with this repository's own HARD RULE that money/PII never reaches a public surface (docs/00-start-here/HANDOFF.md). This is why the review is required on the merits, not merely because a prior review round asked for it: a privileged deployment surface's logging behavior changed, and the change was motivated by a real, previously-mismeasured PII exposure path. The fix in this registration (see negative_scope) is an explicit field allowlist at the CLI sink. As originally shipped this round it kept {code/severity/constraint/table/column/routine/file/line} and dropped row-shaped ones (detail/hint/internalQuery/where); gate-attempt-03 round 1 [P1] then found constraint/table/column are themselves developer/attacker-settable via PL/pgSQL's RAISE ... USING. gate-attempt-04 round 1 (fourth registration) found `code` is settable the same way (RAISE...USING ERRCODE). Fifth registration: the allowlist keeps only {severity/routine/file/line} -- fields never settable by any SQL statement, per the provenance rule in negative_scope, not a per-field safety argument. `.cause` itself is unchanged and correct. NOTE FOR THE REVIEWER: the measurement above (2026-08-01, round 1 of this registration) covered the unique_violation/23505 shape only, via `.cause.detail`. This registration's own round 2 later the same day found a SECOND, independent exposure path this reason does not describe: for a data-exception class like 22P02, the offending value sits directly in the PRIMARY message, not `.detail` -- the wrapping `.message` itself was not safe to print either. Both paths are now closed (formatMigrationFailureForLog no longer prints any free-text message, from any source, plus a safeLogSummary mechanism that preserves only pre-vetted-safe context). Do not treat the measurement in this paragraph as the complete picture -- verify against `packages/db/src/migrate.test.ts`'s "CLI failure-log sink" tests directly, which are the current, authoritative account of every failure shape measured and how each is handled.
